answer_text:
Here is a comprehensive guide to the **best sources for free 3D game assets** in 2026:

---

## 🎮 Top Sites for Free 3D Game Assets

### 1. 🏆 [Kenney.nl](https://kenney.nl)
This one-person operation has released over 40,000 assets — all CC0, all free, no sign-up required. The art style is clean, colourful, and remarkably consistent across packs, which means you can mix and match assets without your game looking inconsistent. The site offers 2D assets, 3D models, UI elements, fonts, and audio. There are also free tools like **Asset Forge** for creating your own 3D models.

---

### 2. 🎨 [Quaternius](https://quaternius.com)
If you're making a 3D game with a stylised low-poly look, Quaternius is essential. This Argentinian artist has released thousands of models — characters, animals, vehicles, environments, weapons — all under CC0. The signature "Quaternius style" is instantly recognisable: clean geometry, bright colours, charming animations. Assets come rigged and animated, ready to drop into Unity, Unreal, or Godot.

---

### 3. 🌍 [PolyHaven](https://polyhaven.com)
Poly Haven started as HDRI Haven and has grown into a comprehensive library of 3D models, HDRIs, and textures — all CC0. The models tend toward realistic props and environmental pieces rather than stylised game assets, but they're high quality and instantly usable. No sign-up required — just download what you need.

---

### 4. 🖼️ [Sketchfab](https://sketchfab.com)
Sketchfab is a huge repository of 3D models, and it has a large collection of downloadable assets. While many are for sale, there's a substantial number of models available for free. The platform's built-in 3D viewer is a great feature, allowing you to inspect every angle of a model before you download it. Just be sure to check the licensing for each model, as they can vary.

---

### 5. 🕹️ [itch.io](https://itch.io/game-assets/free/tag-3d)
Itch.io is a popular platform for indie game developers to host and sell their games, but it also has a massive section for game assets. You can find a wide variety of free 3D game assets, from character models to environmental packs, often with very permissive licenses. The community-driven nature of Itch.io means you'll discover unique and creative assets you won't find anywhere else.

---

### 6. 🎭 [Mixamo](https://mixamo.com) *(Animations)*
Mixamo offers **2,000+ free animations** with auto-rigging, making it perfect for character animation without needing to rig from scratch.

---

### 7. 🏪 [Unity Asset Store (Free Section)](https://assetstore.unity.com)
The Unity Asset Store is an essential resource for anyone developing with the Unity engine. It offers **10,000+ Unity-optimized assets** in its free section.

---

### 8. 🌐 [OpenGameArt](https://opengameart.org)
OpenGameArt has been around for over a decade and hosts a massive collection of 2D art, 3D models, music, and sound effects — all under open licences like CC0, CC-BY, or GPL.

---

### 9. 🔬 [Quixel Megascans](https://quixel.com)
Quixel is releasing a final, offline version of Quixel Mixer, along with the option to download over **800 free Quixel Megascans assets**. It's a pioneer in the creation of photogrammetry-based 3D assets, delivering photorealistic models compatible with any engine. All assets are scanned from real-world objects using purpose-built hardware and meticulously processed for the highest-fidelity results.

---

### 10. 🆓 [Free3D](https://free3d.com)
A large number of the recent models have a lower polygon count and can be used in games straight away, covering subcategories like House, Building, Medieval, Fantasy, City, Tower, and Bridge. For game development, Free3D also hosts several low poly models made specifically for real-time usage.

---

### 11. 🎨 [ArtStation Marketplace](https://artstation.com/marketplace)
ArtStation has a popular marketplace full of nearly 60,000 assets. There are a ton of high-quality free game assets in all kinds of styles. Not just limited to meshes and artwork, the assets also include custom-built textures and elements like clothing and hair.

---

## 📄 Understanding Licenses

Here's a quick breakdown:
- **CC0 (Public Domain)** — ✅ Use commercially, ✅ Modify freely, ✅ No attribution required
- **CC BY (Attribution)** — ✅ Use commercially, ✅ Modify freely, ⚠️ Must credit original creator
- **CC BY-SA** — ✅ Use commercially, ✅ Modify freely, ⚠️ Must credit + share modifications under same license

---

## 💡 Pro Tips

For style consistency: choose assets from the same creator or pack (e.g., all Quaternius or all Kenney), don't mix photorealistic and low-poly cartoon styles, and use unified lighting with consistent HDRI skyboxes from PolyHaven.

**Best file formats:** GLB/glTF are recommended because all textures, materials, and animations are bundled in one file, with 3–5x faster loading compared to FBX with separate textures, and native support in Three.js, Babylon.js, Unity, and Unreal Engine.
